A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPAM optimizer. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, algorithms, tables and figures, allowing reliable comparison despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient analyses, simulations, LLM training experiments, quantization-aware training, reinforcement learning, vision evaluations and weather forecasting results.

after.justification: v2 retains original gradient analyses, simulations, LLM pre-training and fine-tuning results, vision evaluations, weather forecasting and multiple ablation studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same periodic moment reset, cosine warmup, second-moment-based spike clipping and random sparse-momentum selection. Removing '(Sparse)' from the Table 3 label does not change the described procedure.

E1.justification: v2 removes the reinforcement-learning task family covering Ant-V4, HalfCheetah-V4 and Hopper-V2. Weather forecasting remains and gains a severity-10 corruption scenario beyond severities 2 and 5. The retained language and ImageNet coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The LLaMA-130M comparison against SPAM without momentum reset in v1 Table 18 disappears. The no-clipping condition remains in the threshold sweep as 'None'. Comparator membership in the retained main benchmarks and other matched appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 removes the complete W4A4/W8A8 quantization-aware evaluation protocol for LLaMA-60M, 130M and 350M, along with the PPO evaluation protocol. Retained LLM training budgets, architectures, learning-rate settings and fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged; Weather evaluation adds the stronger corruption setting.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix L/Table 18, which directly separates momentum reset and spike clipping on LLaMA-130M, is removed, although the no-clipping threshold condition survives. v2 Figure 8 extends Weather robustness testing to severity 10. The other sensitivity, subset-selection and clipping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Removing the RL experiment also removes its five-run averaging statement and shaded variability plots. Both versions retain ten-run mean and standard deviation reporting for fine-tuning and ten repeated Weather runs. The additional Weather panel introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The QAT and RL learning curves disappear, as does the explicit component-ablation table, including the no-reset perplexity of 24.32. New severity-10 Weather curves favor SPAM over Adam. Matched retained tables and the three earlier Weather curves are unchanged; standard SPAM pre-training perplexities remain 30.46, 23.36, 17.42 and 14.66.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1, the preliminary Adam/AMSGrad regret-bound reasoning in Section 2.3, its assumptions and caveats, and the Gaussian-clipping formulation are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces explicit superiority claims spanning LLM training, low-bit training, RL and forecasting with superiority across model scales. The contribution list similarly drops the task enumeration. The central claims about gradient spikes, SPAM and sparse momentum remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The low-bit applicability interpretation and RL generalization argument in v1 Sections 4.3–4.4 disappear. Explanations of momentum contamination, random subset selection and Weather robustness, together with the convexity and bounded-gradient limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the QAT hyperparameter block and v1 Table 10. This also loses explicit learning rates for retained Weather and vision experiments, respectively 1e-3 and 4e-3, plus task-specific Weather reset and warmup settings. Core pseudocode, LLM configuration details and the code-access link remain.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a paragraph citing Sun et al. (2025), The Curse of Depth, and Li et al. (2024b), Mix-LN. The Schulman et al. (2017) PPO reference disappears with RL. The broader positioning against architectural stabilization, earlier momentum resets and memory-efficient optimizers is retained.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in the experimental narrative: Weather moves to Appendix G, duplicated main-text vision material is removed, and QAT/RL subsections disappear. Affiliations, abstract wording and acknowledgments are revised, while most prose and the top-level section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference typography and extensively redistributes displays. Figure 1 contracts from nine panels to three; the Weather figure moves to the appendix and is redrawn with four panels, new colors and epoch labels. The duplicate vision table, auxiliary hyperparameter table and component-ablation table disappear.

improvement.justification: The additional severe-noise Weather test and removal of duplicated vision material provide modest benefits. However, deleting the direct LLaMA-130M component ablation and explicit settings for retained Weather and vision evaluations weakens component attribution and reproducibility. These losses outweigh the presentation gains, while the unchanged core method and main LLM evidence keep the deterioration limited.
